# awskmscrypto

```go
import "github.com/effective-security/xpki/v2/cryptoprov/awskmscrypto"
```

Package awskmscrypto implements cryptoprov.Provider and cryptoprov.KeyManager over AWS KMS asymmetric signing keys \(RSA 2048/3072/4096, NIST P\-256, P\-384, P\-521 and ML\-DSA\-44/65/87\). It registers itself as manufacturer "AWSKMS". Credentials, the default region and retries come from the default AWS SDK chain. Keys never leave KMS: ExportKey returns a pkcs11: URI and Sign calls kms:Sign with a digest, after checking the options against the algorithms KMS reports for the key. Encryption keys \(cryptoprov.KeyUsageEncrypt, ENCRYPT\_DECRYPT\) are not supported.

The token config Attributes field carries comma separated "Name=value" settings, all optional:

- Endpoint=\<url\> and Region=\<region\> select the KMS endpoint;
- TagSearch=true answers a tag filter with the Resource Groups Tagging API and makes GenerateKey write the xpki\-label, xpki\-type, xpki\-size and xpki\-usage tags \(TaggingEndpoint=\<url\> is the endpoint of that API\). It needs tag:GetResources and kms:TagResource;
- LabelSearch=scan makes a label filter describe every key and match its description, instead of looking the label up through its alias;
- DescribeConcurrency=\<n\> is the number of per\-key requests a listing has in flight at once \(1 to 64, default 8\);
- MetadataCacheSize=\<n\> is the number of keys whose immutable metadata the provider remembers \(default 50000, 0 disables\).

ListKeys needs kms:ListKeys, kms:DescribeKey and kms:ListAliases, and kms:ListResourceTags when it reads tags without TagSearch. KMS has no search: Provider.ListKeys describes how a listing narrows its candidates \(the alias of a label, the tagging API, cached key metadata\) before it describes a key, and what each filter costs.

```
req := &cryptoprov.ListKeysRequest{
	Filter: cryptoprov.KeyFilter{
		LabelPrefix: "issuer-",
		Usage:       cryptoprov.KeyUsageSign,
	},
	Fields: cryptoprov.KeyFieldMetadata,
}
for key, err := range cryptoprov.AllKeys(ctx, provider, req) {
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fmt.Println(key.ID, key.Label, key.Type, key.Size)
}
```

```go
func NewSigner(keyID string, label string, signingAlgorithms []types.SigningAlgorithmSpec, publicKey crypto.PublicKey, kmsClient KmsClient) crypto.Signer
```

NewSigner creates a signer for the KMS key keyID. signingAlgorithms are the algorithms KMS reports for the key \(KeyMetadata.SigningAlgorithms or GetPublicKeyOutput.SigningAlgorithms\); Sign accepts only those, so a key without any, such as an ENCRYPT\_DECRYPT key, can not sign.

## type [Provider](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/cryptoprov/awskmscrypto/awskmsprov.go#L317-L334>)

Provider implements cryptoprov.Provider and cryptoprov.KeyManager for AWS KMS: the keys of one account and Region. It is safe for concurrent use.

<a name="Init"></a>
### func [Init](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/cryptoprov/awskmscrypto/awskmsprov.go#L346>)

```go
func Init(tc cryptoprov.TokenConfig) (*Provider, error)
```

Init creates a provider for tc. Its Attributes may carry "Endpoint=\<url\>" and "Region=\<region\>", and the listing settings "TagSearch=true" \(with "TaggingEndpoint=\<url\>"\), "LabelSearch=scan", "DescribeConcurrency=\<n\>" and "MetadataCacheSize=\<n\>", which ListKeys describes; an invalid value is an error. Credentials, the default region and retries come from the default AWS SDK chain, which reads AWS\_ACCESS\_KEY\_ID, AWS\_SECRET\_ACCESS\_KEY and AWS\_SESSION\_TOKEN before the shared config, so the provider does not copy them into a static provider of its own \(XPKI\-034\). The clients from KmsClientFactory and TaggingClientFactory make no request until a key operation.

<a name="Provider.GenerateKey"></a>
### func \(\*Provider\) [GenerateKey](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/cryptoprov/awskmscrypto/awskmsprov.go#L449>)

```go
func (p *Provider) GenerateKey(ctx context.Context, req *cryptoprov.GenerateKeyRequest) (crypto.PrivateKey, error)
```

GenerateKey creates a KMS signing key as req describes it: RSA of 2048, 3072 or 4096 bits, ECDSA on P\-256, P\-384 or P\-521, or ML\-DSA\-44, 65 or 87 \(key spec ML\_DSA\_\*\), with req.Label as its description and alias and req.Tags as its tags, and returns its Signer. With the TagSearch attribute it also writes the xpki\-label, xpki\-type, xpki\-size and xpki\-usage tags that let a listing skip DescribeKey; tags need kms:TagResource, and a tag name that starts with "xpki\-" is reserved.

An ML\-DSA signer signs messages through the EXTERNAL\_MU operation: μ is computed locally, so the message never leaves the process and the RAW message size limit of KMS does not apply; see cryptoprov.MLDSASignerOptions for the options it accepts. This provider has no decrypter, so cryptoprov.KeyUsageEncrypt is a wrapped cryptoprov.ErrNotSupported before any request \(XPKI\-031\), as is a size KMS does not offer.

<a name="Provider.GetKey"></a>
### func \(\*Provider\) [GetKey](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/cryptoprov/awskmscrypto/awskmsprov.go#L667>)

```go
func (p *Provider) GetKey(ctx context.Context, keyID string) (crypto.PrivateKey, error)
```

GetKey returns the Signer of the KMS key keyID \(a key id, ARN, alias name or alias ARN\), labelled with the key description. The key usage must be SIGN\_VERIFY, otherwise the error wraps cryptoprov.ErrNotSupported, and the key must not be pending deletion: neither can sign, so no signer is returned for them \(XPKI\-031\). A disabled key gets a signer, since it can be enabled again; its Sign fails until then. A key KMS does not have is a wrapped cryptoprov.ErrKeyNotFound.

<a name="Provider.KeyInfo"></a>
### func \(\*Provider\) [KeyInfo](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/cryptoprov/awskmscrypto/awskmsprov.go#L798>)

```go
func (p *Provider) KeyInfo(ctx context.Context, keyID string, fields cryptoprov.KeyFields) (*cryptoprov.KeyInfo, error)
```

KeyInfo describes the key keyID \(a key id, ARN, alias name or alias ARN\) with one DescribeKey, which supplies the Metadata and State groups whatever fields selects. cryptoprov.KeyFieldTags adds the tags \(ListResourceTags, which needs kms:ListResourceTags\) and cryptoprov.KeyFieldPublicKey the PEM public key \(GetPublicKey\). A key KMS does not have is a wrapped cryptoprov.ErrKeyNotFound.

<a name="Provider.ListKeys"></a>
### func \(\*Provider\) [ListKeys](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/cryptoprov/awskmscrypto/listkeys.go#L184>)

```go
func (p *Provider) ListKeys(ctx context.Context, req *cryptoprov.ListKeysRequest) (*cryptoprov.ListKeysResponse, error)
```

ListKeys returns one page of the keys of the account and Region.

KMS has no search, so the call first picks a source of candidates:

- a tag filter with the TagSearch attribute: GetResources of the Resource Groups Tagging API, 100 keys a page, each with its tags \(tag:GetResources\);
- a label filter: DescribeKey on the alias of an exact label, or a ListAliases sweep for a prefix \(kms:ListAliases\), followed with TagSearch by the keys the xpki\-label tag names. The label of a key is its description, which every candidate is confirmed against, so a key is found through the alias GenerateKey gave it; a key that has only a matching description is not found unless the LabelSearch=scan attribute makes the listing describe every key, as v1 did;
- otherwise ListKeys, 1000 ids a page \(kms:ListKeys\).

It then makes only the requests the filter and req.Fields need, at most DescribeConcurrency at a time; the first failure cancels the rest and is returned wrapped, so errors.As still finds the service error, and there is no partial page \(XPKI\-033\). A listing of ids without a filter makes none. Key spec, usage, creation date, origin and manager never change, so a filter on usage or type costs one DescribeKey the first time the provider sees a key and none afterwards \(MetadataCacheSize\). The label and the state can change and are read with DescribeKey \(kms:DescribeKey\) for the keys of the page; a key from the tagging API that has the xpki tags needs none for cryptoprov.KeyFieldMetadata, and is then listed without a creation time unless the provider described it before. Tags that the source did not return cost one ListResourceTags per key \(kms:ListResourceTags\). The xpki tags can be written by anyone with kms:TagResource: they feed listings only, never GetKey, KeyInfo or Sign.

A call examines at most one page of its source, so a page can have fewer keys than req.PageSize, or none, and still a NextPageToken. A key the caller may not describe \(AccessDeniedException\), or that is gone, is not listed and is logged. Keys pending deletion are listed unless req.Filter.States excludes them.

<a name="Signer.Sign"></a>
### func \(\*Signer\) [Sign](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/cryptoprov/awskmscrypto/signer.go#L120>)

```go
func (s *Signer) Sign(rand io.Reader, digest []byte, opts crypto.SignerOpts) (signature []byte, err error)
```

Sign signs digest with the KMS key. For an RSA or ECDSA key opts is required \(XPKI\-025\): its hash selects the KMS algorithm and digest must have that hash's length. \*rsa.PSSOptions select RSASSA\_PSS for an RSA key and are rejected for an ECDSA key; the salt must be rsa.PSSSaltLengthEqualsHash or the hash size, the only salt KMS produces \(rsa.PSSSaltLengthAuto asks for a maximal salt and is rejected\). The algorithm must be one the key supports, as KMS reported when the signer was created; for an ECDSA key that is the algorithm of its curve.

An ML\-DSA key signs the message: digest is the message with nil, a zero hash or \*mldsa.Options, or the 64\-byte representative μ with crypto.MLDSAMu \(cryptoprov.MLDSASignerOptions\); every other hash is an error. The signer computes μ locally and calls KMS with MessageType EXTERNAL\_MU and ML\_DSA\_SHAKE\_256, so the message itself is never sent. Invalid options fail before any RPC.
